scope: A public-safe comparative chapter extending the four-case anchor. It follows operating mechanisms across venture models, data infrastructure, developer adoption, accelerator-backed wedges and country conditions. It is not a company census or a venture recommendation.

opening.title: The useful unit is a mechanism, not a logo.
opening.dek: The next question after the four anchor cases is what sits between a listing and a result: who pays, who does the work, what the company carries, and which country conditions make the promise possible.
opening.boundary: Numbers below keep their source period, currency and evidence label. Company claims are not silently upgraded into measured outcomes.

lenses.title: Managed brokerage and new-home distribution
lenses.question: Who owns the handoff when a listing has to become a transaction?
lenses.summary: The strongest operators do not remove field work. They make roles, records, licences, visits, negotiation and collection legible enough for people to cooperate.
lenses.transfer: Bangladesh would need a small, written role and fee system that survives an offline closing before a national network claim is responsible.

cases.name: KE Holdings / Beike
cases.mechanism: Agent Cooperation Network plus developer sales
cases.customer: Existing-home buyers and sellers, connected brokerage brands and developers.
cases.payer: Commission at closing, platform and franchise services, and developer sales commissions.
cases.workflow: A listing owner or store supplies inventory, an agent brings demand, roles are allocated through ACN, visits and negotiation are logged, then the transaction centre allocates commission.
cases.human_burden: Listing authenticity, agent training, conduct enforcement, local visits, transaction coordination and developer receivable follow-up.
cases.journey: Lianjia's store network became an open platform in 2018. The 2024 filing reports about 445,000 active agents, 49,000 active stores and about 75% of existing-home sales involving cross-store collaboration.
cases.monetization: 2024 net revenue was RMB93.5bn and GTV was RMB3,349.4bn. New-home transaction-service revenue was RMB33.653bn, with RMB8.349bn of reported contribution after defined variable costs.
cases.result: Observed in an audited filing and results exhibit. GTV is not revenue, and contribution is not consolidated operating profit.
cases.capital: Working capital includes developer receivables of about RMB5.9bn and deposits of about RMB0.5bn at 31 December 2024.
cases.failure_or_limit: The filing flags housing-cycle, developer-credit, listing-quality, privacy and regulatory risks. ACN causality is not isolated.
cases.unknown: Agent income, retention, enforcement cost and Bangladesh-level network density are not disclosed.
cases.transfer_test: Can two independent participants complete and reconcile a defined set of transactions under a role and commission rule they trust?

cases.name: Compass
cases.mechanism: Licensed principal brokerage with independent agents
cases.customer: Home buyers and sellers represented by affiliated agents.
cases.payer: Client-side commission recognised when a transaction closes.
cases.workflow: Agents affiliate their licences with Compass, market and show property, coordinate disclosures, negotiate and close under the brokerage licence.
cases.human_burden: Licensing supervision, recruiting, lead generation, pricing, showings, negotiation, inspection and closing coordination remain human work.
cases.journey: The 2024 filing reports 205,122 transactions, $216.8bn GTV and 17,752 principal agents at year end.
cases.monetization: 2024 revenue was $5.6291bn. Commissions and related expense was $4.6346bn, or 82.3% of revenue. Revenue is not earned for a failed closing.
cases.result: Observed public-company scale and cost structure, not a benchmark take rate for Bangladesh.
cases.capital: The balance sheet carries brokerage infrastructure and acquisition history, while the main economic exposure is agent compensation and sales expense rather than owned homes.
cases.failure_or_limit: The model depends on licence rules, agent supply and transactions closing. Software does not remove the principal's legal or collection obligations.
cases.unknown: Dhaka licensing, agent split, tax and failed-deal economics have not been established.
cases.transfer_test: Would a named Bangladesh principal accept responsibility for the same workflow and fee event, with a documented split and failed-deal rule?

cases.name: QuintoAndar
cases.mechanism: Managed rental and sales workflow with partner agencies
cases.customer: Owners, tenants, buyers, sellers and partner agencies.
cases.payer: Brokerage and administration fees, plus protection and related services.
cases.workflow: The platform sources property, handles contracts and payment, coordinates inspections and claims, and routes some listings or visits through partner agencies.
cases.human_burden: Screening, contract execution, collections, inspections, mediation, protection claims and partner-conduct monitoring.
cases.journey: A June 2025 newsroom release reported R$20bn one-year transaction value and 300,000 managed rental contracts. A 2026 release describes a Domi AI workflow, commission recovery and broker removals.
cases.monetization: Current help guidance describes a one-month brokerage fee and a 9.3% administration fee with a R$160 minimum, subject to contract and market terms.
cases.result: Product and company-reported scale are visible. Transaction value is not revenue, and partner-sales growth has no disclosed control or denominator.
cases.capital: Protection and guaranteed-payment products create claims, reserves, payment and operating exposure even when the platform does not own the home.
cases.failure_or_limit: QuintoCred Garantia was closed in 2025 as the company concentrated the business. The source does not disclose product P&L or loss ratios.
cases.unknown: Bangladesh arrears, inspection, insurance, damage and anti-bypass economics are untested.
cases.transfer_test: Can a local rental or new-home service write a collection, protection and exception rule that a payer will fund?

cases.name: NoBroker
cases.mechanism: Broker-free discovery with paid assisted execution
cases.customer: Owners, tenants, buyers and sellers using discovery or assisted plans.
cases.payer: Customers pay for visible plans and transaction support rather than a traditional broker percentage.
cases.workflow: Requirement intake, calling, field assistance, visits, showings, negotiation and relationship-manager support sit behind the broker-free message.
cases.human_burden: Local calling, property visits, showing coordination, negotiation and refunds or service recovery.
cases.journey: The live plan pages make the paid assistance and field workflow visible. The company also reported a US$210m 2021 Series E and a 2025 brokerage-saved figure.
cases.monetization: The service proposition is plan-based and assisted. The 2025 report claimed INR7,200 crore brokerage saved, but gives no transaction denominator or counterfactual fee rule.
cases.result: The payer tension is the evidence: broker-free positioning can coexist with paid human work. Commercial conversion and profit remain unknown.
cases.capital: The funding round shows capital access, not contribution margin or customer payback.
cases.failure_or_limit: The brokerage-saved claim is not an audited outcome. A live page also does not prove repeat use or completed transactions.
cases.unknown: Dhaka willingness to pay for assisted plans, field cost and conversion from discovery to collection.
cases.transfer_test: Will a customer prepay for one bounded action, and can the action be fulfilled without recreating an informal brokerage?

cases.name: Square Yards
cases.mechanism: Developer and channel-partner distribution with mortgage adjacencies
cases.customer: Developers, channel partners, buyers, banks/NBFCs and property owners.
cases.payer: Developer sales commissions, financial-product or service relationships and adjacent property services.
cases.workflow: Project onboarding, lead registration, partner assignment, visits, booking, mortgage and payout reconciliation.
cases.human_burden: Project data, partner governance, field visits, booking exceptions, financing documents and collection from developers.
cases.journey: The product surface spans developers, agents, consumers, mortgage, management and data. Its FY25 release reported consolidated revenue, GTV, transactions and positive operating cash flow.
cases.monetization: FY25 company figures included INR1,410 crore revenue, INR59,093 crore GTV and more than 186,000 transactions. No segment split is supplied.
cases.result: A new-home channel can be commercially meaningful without owning inventory, but the cited figures are consolidated and company-reported.
cases.capital: The channel carries lead, partner, payout and working-capital exposure. Funding is a capital event, not proof of return.
cases.failure_or_limit: Definitions and audit of network counts, deal counts and payouts are not disclosed. Mortgage and management lines may have different economics.
cases.unknown: Bangladesh developer concentration, payout ageing and channel neutrality.
cases.transfer_test: Can one project provide a signed channel agreement, lead-to-booking funnel and collected payout record?

cases.name: PropTiger / Housing.com inside REA India
cases.mechanism: Full-stack new-home and portal portfolio, then a line and ownership reset
cases.customer: Developers, buyers, brokers and portal advertisers across different lines.
cases.payer: Developer and portal revenue streams with distinct reporting boundaries.
cases.workflow: Search, virtual viewing, site visits, diligence, negotiation, registration, loans and post-sale support were described across the historical combination.
cases.human_burden: Developer relationships, sales support, compliance, registration, lead generation and separating line-level reporting.
cases.journey: REA later disclosed PropTiger revenue down 17% in FY25 and broadly EBITDA breakeven. The sale to Aurum completed 25 September 2025. Housing Edge was discontinued after a regulatory change.
cases.monetization: FY25 revenue and EBITDA of A$74.5m and A$12.7m were for combined PropTiger plus Housing Edge, not PropTiger alone.
cases.result: The material outcome is identity discipline: a portfolio can contain a meaningful channel and still require divestiture, discontinuation and denominator correction.
cases.capital: The divestiture completed for INR865m of Aurum shares representing 5.5% equity, with an approximately A$4.5m gain for REA.
cases.failure_or_limit: Post-transfer Aurum-owned PropTiger operating data is not in the reopened set. The cited history does not prove a single causal failure.
cases.unknown: Current PropTiger margins, customer retention and integration after transfer.
cases.transfer_test: Would a parent-backed channel separate brand, ownership, payer and reporting line before presenting scale?

lenses.title: Rentals, property management and home services
lenses.question: What happens after the transaction, when the promise repeats every month?
lenses.summary: Rent collection, guarantees, maintenance and fulfilment turn a marketplace into a service operation. Recurring revenue also creates recurring exceptions, claims and quality control.
lenses.transfer: A Bangladesh test needs a defined service area, responsible field partner, collection path, repair standard and loss or rework rule.

cases.name: QuintoAndar managed rentals
cases.mechanism: Administration fee plus payment and protection workflow
cases.customer: Owners and tenants in managed rental contracts.
cases.payer: Owners and tenants through brokerage, administration and guarantee terms.
cases.workflow: Screen, contract, schedule rent and IPTU payment, inspect entry and exit, mediate and manage covered events.
cases.human_burden: Collection, inspection, claims, repair or damage decisions, tenant support and contract enforcement.
cases.journey: The company reported 300,000 managed rental contracts in June 2025 and later announced Benvi to acquire rights to manage active contracts from local agencies.
cases.monetization: A current help page describes 9.3% administration fees with a minimum, plus a one-month brokerage fee, subject to contract.
cases.result: Recurring management is a product and operating system, not a passive subscription. Scale is company-reported.
cases.capital: Payment guarantees and protection require contractual reserves or risk partners. QuintoCred's 2025 closure shows the line can be strategically reset.
cases.failure_or_limit: No audited claims-loss, retention or contribution data is disclosed in the selected sources.
cases.unknown: Whether landlords in Dhaka would fund a comparable fee and protection layer.
cases.transfer_test: Can a pilot collect rent or fees on time for a small managed cohort while recording arrears, repairs and rework?

cases.name: Houm
cases.mechanism: Managed rental administration with field operations
cases.customer: Landlords and tenants seeking rental placement and administration.
cases.payer: Rental administration and related transaction services.
cases.workflow: Find property, screen, visit, place tenant, collect rent and support administration.
cases.human_burden: Local visits, landlord acquisition, screening, rent operations and service recovery across multiple countries.
cases.journey: A 2023 Forbes Colombia interview described a hard market, a focus on recurring administration and a near-profitability statement, alongside a reported 250-properties-per-day metric.
cases.monetization: Recurring administration is the core described model; the interview does not disclose audited revenue or margin.
cases.result: The case suggests a rental operator can target repeat administration, but the public evidence is founder-reported.
cases.capital: Field density and local operations are the main visible burden; funding and loss exposure are not fully disclosed.
cases.failure_or_limit: The source does not give cohort retention, unit economics or country-level margins.
cases.unknown: A Dhaka rental operator's cost to screen, inspect, collect and resolve disputes.
cases.transfer_test: What minimum managed cohort makes a field team and collection process economically repeatable?

cases.name: AppFolio
cases.mechanism: Property-management system of record plus payments and risk services
cases.customer: Professional property managers and their owners or tenants.
cases.payer: Subscription customers plus usage-based payments, screening and risk-mitigation services.
cases.workflow: Maintain property records, lease and tenant workflows, collect payments, screen applicants, integrate services and report.
cases.human_burden: Customer implementation, support, compliance, payment exceptions and third-party integration management.
cases.journey: The 2024 10-K reported $794.2m revenue, 20,784 customers and 8.7m units, with 6% unit growth.
cases.monetization: Subscription plus usage-based fees. The filing identifies third-party dependencies and $6.7m of deposits tied to a risk-mitigation service.
cases.result: A recurring property-management system can scale when the customer is a professional operator. It is not evidence that maintenance margins transfer.
cases.capital: Payments, screening, insurance and deposits create operational and compliance exposure without owning buildings.
cases.failure_or_limit: US law, customer concentration and vendor dependencies differ from Bangladesh. Product-level margin is not isolated.
cases.unknown: A local property manager's willingness to pay for software before a dependable record exists.
cases.transfer_test: Can a local operator keep a complete lease, payment and maintenance record for one portfolio and renew it?

cases.name: Urban Company
cases.mechanism: Managed home-service marketplace with trained partners
cases.customer: Households buying scheduled home services.
cases.payer: Customers pay for a service; the platform coordinates partner fulfilment and quality.
cases.workflow: Request, match, schedule, train or certify provider, fulfil, handle warranty or rework and pay partner.
cases.human_burden: Training, safety, partner support, quality control, insurance and service recovery.
cases.journey: FY2024 materials reported INR827 crore revenue and a PBT loss of INR93 crore, with partner-training and protection initiatives.
cases.monetization: Service transaction revenue with partner economics and category-specific costs.
cases.result: Demand and operational scale can coexist with a reported loss. The platform's promise is fulfilment, not listing volume.
cases.capital: Training, insurance, loans and service recovery require operating capital and governance.
cases.failure_or_limit: The reported figures are company disclosures and do not isolate category or city margin.
cases.unknown: Whether property maintenance in Dhaka can reach enough density to cover a trained field network.
cases.transfer_test: Can one service category meet a written response, rework and payment standard at a positive contribution?

cases.name: Sheba Platform
cases.mechanism: Local service aggregation with training and payment infrastructure
cases.customer: Households and businesses ordering local services.
cases.payer: Service customers and participating providers through transaction and payment workflows.
cases.workflow: Acquire demand, route to providers, train or certify, fulfil, collect and resolve quality issues.
cases.human_burden: Local provider recruitment, training, quality assurance, customer support and payment operations.
cases.journey: Reported interviews describe a COVID pause, a 2022 funding crisis, layoffs and later arrears repayment. A trade-body profile records dated service and provider claims.
cases.monetization: The selected sources describe transaction and payment infrastructure, but not audited current segment margins.
cases.result: The local comparator makes financing and fulfilment stress visible. Its reported scale is not proof of a property-specific opportunity.
cases.capital: Working capital and arrears management matter. The 2023 report described Tk7 crore of arrears paid after the crisis period.
cases.failure_or_limit: Current financial status and profitability are not independently established in the selected records.
cases.unknown: A property-specific service cohort, repeat rate and service-level cost.
cases.transfer_test: Can JCX define one property service where the provider, customer, quality and collection records are all visible?

lenses.title: Verification, property data and transaction infrastructure
lenses.question: What makes a property fact trustworthy enough for someone to pay for it?
lenses.summary: A verified record is a chain of source, identifier, definition, exception handling and responsibility. A portal badge is not automatically a registry fact.
lenses.transfer: The first Bangladesh product should be rights-aware and workflow-bound, with a named payer and a clearly limited assurance level.

cases.name: HM Land Registry
cases.mechanism: Public title register and Price Paid Data
cases.customer: Homeowners, buyers, lenders, conveyancers, researchers and data companies.
cases.payer: Fees for official copies, register-change services and professional information services.
cases.workflow: Professionals submit applications, caseworkers resolve requisitions, the register changes, and official records or price data are published under stated rules.
cases.human_burden: Legal review, identity and fraud controls, queues, staff capacity, corrections and service-level management.
cases.journey: The 2024-25 report records £399.2m total revenue, about 19,000 daily update or title-creation requests and 4.43m register-change applications processed.
cases.monetization: Information services generated £27.6m and official copies about £81.9m in the cited year. These are public-service revenues, not venture margins.
cases.result: Public authority, definitions and change controls make the record usable. Price Paid Data still has exclusions and registration lag.
cases.capital: Long-lived infrastructure, trained caseworkers, cybersecurity, legal authority and fraud prevention.
cases.failure_or_limit: The title plan is a general boundary, and the latest price months are incomplete. The source does not promise error-free data.
cases.unknown: Which Bangladesh records can be commercially reused, joined and corrected under a comparable responsibility model.
cases.transfer_test: Can a defined property record name its source, date, identifier, reviewer, rights and correction route?

cases.name: Dubai Land Department and Dubai Pulse
cases.mechanism: Government transaction data with machine-readable publication metadata
cases.customer: Public agencies, market participants, researchers and downstream data products.
cases.payer: Public-service access and downstream commercial or professional use under stated rights and credentials.
cases.workflow: DLD records transactions, rents, projects, valuations, land, units, brokers and developers; Dubai Pulse publishes dataset provenance, fields and update metadata.
cases.human_burden: Government record maintenance, permissions, privacy, source governance and downstream interpretation.
cases.journey: The open-data pages and 2026 dataset metadata expose the breadth and update cadence of the institutional rail.
cases.monetization: The selected public records do not establish downstream product margins or a private data subscription price.
cases.result: An official-data rail changes what a platform can query and compare. It does not make every estimate a title certificate.
cases.capital: Institutional data infrastructure and governance sit upstream of private interfaces.
cases.failure_or_limit: Access, field coverage, privacy and licence conditions differ from Bangladesh.
cases.unknown: Whether an equivalent Bangladesh source can be accessed, refreshed and reused for a paying decision-maker.
cases.transfer_test: Can a local data product state exactly which government field it uses and what the field does not prove?

cases.name: India DILRMP and ULPIN
cases.mechanism: Land-record modernisation, cadastral mapping and parcel identifiers
cases.customer: State land departments, registries, citizens and institutions using land records.
cases.payer: Public budgets and service fees, not a single commercial subscription.
cases.workflow: Digitise records, integrate registration and maps, assign identifiers, publish services and manage state-level implementation.
cases.human_burden: Survey, data cleaning, local administration, legal integration, correction and long programme delivery.
cases.journey: The programme pages show continuing 2021-26 and 2026-31 modernisation work rather than a finished nationwide rail.
cases.monetization: No commercial unit economics are established in the cited programme records.
cases.result: Digitisation and identifiers are infrastructure programmes. They are not proof that every digitised record is current or legally dispositive.
cases.capital: Large public investment, cadastral work, integration and long implementation cycles.
cases.failure_or_limit: State variation, accuracy, legal effect and access remain material.
cases.unknown: The feasible join between Bangladesh khatian, mutation, deed, approval, valuation and unit records.
cases.transfer_test: Which single record join would remove a paid decision bottleneck without pretending to be title assurance?

cases.name: CoStar Group
cases.mechanism: Proprietary research plus recurring professional subscriptions
cases.customer: Professional real-estate investors, brokers, lenders and operators.
cases.payer: Recurring subscribers buying data, research and workflow access.
cases.workflow: Collect, standardise, verify and maintain property and market data, then sell it through professional products with renewals.
cases.human_burden: Research staff, data quality, sales, integrations, support and retention work.
cases.journey: The 2024 10-K describes subscription products, renewal and human-capital requirements. A results release provides a rounded cross-check of company performance.
cases.monetization: Subscription revenue and professional renewal are the core boundary; country-level product margin is not isolated.
cases.result: A durable data business requires proprietary depth and recurring payer value, not just a clean interface.
cases.capital: Research operations, data acquisition, product infrastructure, sales and support.
cases.failure_or_limit: A Dhaka dataset may lack comparable depth, rights and renewal willingness.
cases.unknown: Which local professional would pay repeatedly for a limited but reliable dataset.
cases.transfer_test: Can a named lender, developer or broker renew a narrowly defined data service after seeing its exception log?

cases.name: Beike listing and closing controls
cases.mechanism: Private network verification and role allocation
cases.customer: Agents, stores, buyers, sellers and developers using a coordinated network.
cases.payer: Transaction commissions and platform services.
cases.workflow: Listing information is supplied, checked and governed through the network, while agents and transaction centres handle visits and closing.
cases.human_burden: Verification, monitoring, penalties, training and exception resolution.
cases.journey: The 20-F states that listing information must be reviewed, monitored and verified and cannot be guaranteed perpetually authentic or current.
cases.monetization: Trust controls support a larger transaction and service platform rather than a separately disclosed verification product.
cases.result: Even a scaled network treats verification as ongoing operations, not a one-time badge.
cases.capital: People, stores, data systems and governance.
cases.failure_or_limit: No public product margin isolates verification or ACN enforcement.
cases.unknown: Whether local agents would accept a comparable evidence and penalty system.
cases.transfer_test: Can a local owner, document and freshness record survive a dispute and an agent handoff?

lenses.title: Technology adoption inside developers
lenses.question: What changes when technology is used by an operating company, not sold as a new venture?
lenses.summary: Adoption evidence clusters around records, customer workflows, construction controls and bounded pilots. The public material rarely proves causal ROI, but it does reveal ownership and operating burden.
lenses.transfer: JCX should separate buy, configure, integrate, build and non-software process work, then instrument adoption and exceptions before adding AI.

cases.name: Aldar
cases.mechanism: Digital Spine, CRM consolidation and customer app
cases.customer: Residents, buyers, tenants and internal operating teams.
cases.payer: Internal operating budget and customer relationships, not an external software subscription.
cases.workflow: Consolidate customer and enterprise systems, expose customer services and track app or digital sales use.
cases.human_burden: Data migration, process ownership, support and adoption across a large portfolio.
cases.journey: FY2024 materials reported 4.2m visits, more than 70% customer app use and 92% digital sales agreements, alongside CRM and ERP transformation.
cases.monetization: The cited disclosures do not isolate software revenue or ROI. The value is internal service and transaction workflow.
cases.result: Adoption metrics are visible, but causal savings and customer outcomes are not independently tested.
cases.capital: Enterprise transformation, migration, integration and change management.
cases.failure_or_limit: Visits and app use are not the same as completed service or profit.
cases.unknown: JCX baseline adoption, data quality and owner for each workflow.
cases.transfer_test: Which internal workflow has a named owner, a current record and a measurable service outcome?

cases.name: Godrej Properties
cases.mechanism: e-CRM, app and grievance workflow
cases.customer: Homebuyers and customer-service teams.
cases.payer: Internal developer budget, with value expected through service and retention.
cases.workflow: Capture grievances, route them, record escalation, resolve and expose status through an app or CRM.
cases.human_burden: Customer support, exception ownership, escalation and data maintenance.
cases.journey: The 2024-25 integrated report states 99% of grievances closed and 96% closed without escalation, with a 3.46-day escalation resolution figure.
cases.monetization: No product revenue or app-specific ROI is disclosed.
cases.result: A service workflow can have internal performance measures, but the source is first-party and not a causal evaluation.
cases.capital: CRM implementation, customer-support operations and process ownership.
cases.failure_or_limit: Closure rate does not disclose issue severity, denominator quality or customer satisfaction beyond the reported metric.
cases.unknown: Whether JCX has comparable case taxonomy, ageing and escalation data.
cases.transfer_test: Can a JCX customer issue be assigned, resolved, audited and reopened without a spreadsheet handoff?

cases.name: Ayala Land
cases.mechanism: Modular construction and AI or drone inspection
cases.customer: Internal project teams, contractors and eventual property customers.
cases.payer: Internal construction and quality budget.
cases.workflow: Use modular components and inspection tools, record defects, accept or rework construction and coordinate project delivery.
cases.human_burden: Site adoption, contractor training, inspection interpretation and rework decisions.
cases.journey: The 2024 integrated report reports 46% modular adoption across 84 projects and 99% first-inspection acceptance for the H3Zoom workflow.
cases.monetization: No external software revenue or independent ROI is disclosed.
cases.result: A project technology can reach operational adoption and a quality metric without proving a general cost or schedule effect.
cases.capital: Construction-process change, equipment, data capture and contractor capability.
cases.failure_or_limit: First-inspection acceptance is not the same as whole-project quality or savings.
cases.unknown: Which JCX construction exception is expensive enough to justify a similar change.
cases.transfer_test: Can one repeated site-quality bottleneck be measured before and after a bounded workflow intervention?

cases.name: DLF
cases.mechanism: ERP-integrated workflows and vendor due diligence
cases.customer: Internal finance, procurement, project and vendor teams.
cases.payer: Internal enterprise-technology and control budget.
cases.workflow: Integrate ERP records, automate dashboards, perform vendor due diligence and move toward SAP S/4HANA.
cases.human_burden: Master data, approvals, controls, migration and user adoption.
cases.journey: The 2024-25 annual report describes the workflow and transition, but does not report quantified ROI.
cases.monetization: Internal control and process value; no external software revenue.
cases.result: The developer case is a record and control investment, not a claim that a new app will create a new business.
cases.capital: ERP implementation, integration, change management and governance.
cases.failure_or_limit: Adoption and outcome measures are not supplied in the cited pages.
cases.unknown: JCX system-of-record fragmentation, approvals and data ownership.
cases.transfer_test: Which shared master record would remove the most repeated reconciliation work?

cases.name: CapitaLand and JLL signals
cases.mechanism: Portfolio pilots, sustainability initiatives and adoption reality checks
cases.customer: Internal investment, operations and occupier teams.
cases.payer: Internal innovation or transformation budget.
cases.workflow: Run pilots, measure portfolio or sustainability initiatives, and assess whether teams adopt or achieve stated AI goals.
cases.human_burden: Pilot selection, integration, change management, governance and benefits tracking.
cases.journey: CapitaLand's FY2023 presentation separates 63 Innovation Fund pilots from 20 Sustainability X projects and 3 completed pilots. JLL's 2025 survey found only 5% of CRE occupier teams reported achieving all AI goals.
cases.monetization: No comparable external software revenue is shown. The value is internal portfolio performance or capability.
cases.result: Pilot count is not adoption, and survey intent is not a JCX outcome. The evidence supports a measurement discipline, not a universal AI sequence.
cases.capital: Pilot funding, integration and owner time; benefits may remain unproven.
cases.failure_or_limit: JLL's combined survey covers 1,500+ decision-makers across 16 markets, but the occupier subgroup denominator is not disclosed.
cases.unknown: Which JCX pilot has an owner, baseline, adoption measure and stop rule.
cases.transfer_test: Can a pilot be stopped or scaled on an observed service or cost result rather than a demo count?

lenses.title: Accelerator wedges and regional comparators
lenses.question: Which narrow jobs attract capital, and what does the public record still not prove?
lenses.summary: Accelerator and startup profiles are useful discovery signals. The stronger evidence appears when a customer, workflow and outcome are named. Funding alone is not product-market fit.
lenses.transfer: A Bangladesh wedge should be selected by a paid workflow and a data or liability boundary, not by copying a batch profile.

cases.name: PermitFlow
cases.mechanism: Construction permitting automation
cases.customer: Builders and construction teams managing permits.
cases.payer: Subscription customers and project operators.
cases.workflow: Prepare, submit, track and coordinate permit work across jurisdictions.
cases.human_burden: Jurisdiction-specific interpretation, document review, submissions, follow-up and exception handling.
cases.journey: The YC profile establishes product identity. TechCrunch reported a $5.5m seed in 2023 and a $31m Series A in 2024, plus company-reported customer, project and ARR growth claims.
cases.monetization: Subscription or workflow software model; the company declined hard revenue in the cited coverage.
cases.result: The wedge is legible and capital-backed. Commercial results remain company-reported.
cases.capital: Venture funding supports jurisdiction expansion and product development, but funding is not customer payback.
cases.failure_or_limit: No audited revenue, retention or permit-outcome dataset is supplied.
cases.unknown: Bangladesh permit authority variation, document format and willingness to pay.
cases.transfer_test: Can one local approval process be mapped end to end with a named professional buyer and measured turnaround?

cases.name: Snapdocs
cases.mechanism: Digital closing workflow for lenders and settlement partners
cases.customer: Lenders, settlement agents and borrowers.
cases.payer: Professional transaction parties buying workflow and e-closing infrastructure.
cases.workflow: Coordinate documents, e-signing, hybrid closing and lender or settlement review.
cases.human_burden: Identity, compliance, document exceptions, lender adoption and settlement coordination.
cases.journey: The YC profile establishes the product. A customer release reported 75% hybrid digital closing adoption at Zions after one month; another release cites an 18-day faster velocity comparison.
cases.monetization: Enterprise workflow and network model; public unit economics are not disclosed.
cases.result: A named customer implementation provides stronger adoption evidence than a profile, but it is still a customer release and not a universal benchmark.
cases.capital: Platform integration, compliance and enterprise sales.
cases.failure_or_limit: The reported cycle-time comparison does not establish causality or Bangladesh equivalence.
cases.unknown: Whether local lenders, lawyers and registries can support a similar e-closing flow.
cases.transfer_test: Which local closing step has a paying institution, a repeatable document standard and a measurable cycle-time baseline?

cases.name: Rabbet
cases.mechanism: Construction finance workflow
cases.customer: Construction lenders, developers and finance teams.
cases.payer: Professional workflow users; current public revenue is not established.
cases.workflow: Organise draw requests, documents, approvals and construction-finance reporting.
cases.human_burden: Review, exception handling, lender controls and construction-document interpretation.
cases.journey: The YC profile provides product identity and intended workflow, but no public revenue or retention result in the selected source.
cases.monetization: Not disclosed in the selected public profile.
cases.result: Useful as a wedge example, not commercial proof.
cases.capital: Enterprise implementation and domain-specific support are implied; capital requirements are not disclosed.
cases.failure_or_limit: Profile evidence cannot establish deployment, renewal or loss reduction.
cases.unknown: Bangladesh lender, developer and draw-control process.
cases.transfer_test: Can one construction payment or draw review be made auditable enough for a paying professional?

cases.name: Trellis
cases.mechanism: AI agents for short-term-rental operations
cases.customer: Short-term-rental property managers.
cases.payer: Property managers paying for operations software; price is not disclosed.
cases.workflow: Agents connect to property-management and messaging tools, answer guest messages, dispatch and follow up on cleaning and maintenance, coordinate vendors, track costs or claims and send owner updates. Trellis gives a broken-shower repair as an example.
cases.human_burden: Managers supply context and review exceptions; people still handle vendor or guest escalation, cost and claim decisions and any safety-sensitive handoff. Trellis says one customer runs day-to-day operations without a human, but that autonomy claim is not independently audited.
cases.journey: The Spring 2026 YC profile says Trellis reached US$500k ARR across 35 customers and 3,000 listings two months after launch, with about 15% week-over-week growth and one customer reporting no human in day-to-day operations. These are founder/company claims, not audited retention, margin, quality or incident results.
cases.monetization: Not publicly established in the selected profile.
cases.result: The case supports a narrow operator workflow hypothesis, not proof of reliable autonomy, quality or Bangladesh fit.
cases.capital: Model, integration and domain support requirements are not disclosed.
cases.failure_or_limit: A short traction claim does not establish retention or quality.
cases.unknown: Which JCX workflow has a sufficiently bounded record and human reviewer.
cases.transfer_test: Can a JCX pilot automate one low-risk maintenance or tenant-query category while logging human overrides, incidents, time saved and accuracy?

cases.name: Lhoopa
cases.mechanism: Decentralised affordable-housing delivery with equity and debt
cases.customer: Affordable-home buyers and housing-finance partners.
cases.payer: Home buyers, project finance and capital providers.
cases.workflow: Acquire or build affordable homes, use local operations, sell and manage finance or delivery risk.
cases.human_burden: Site selection, construction, local sales, financing, collections and decentralised operations.
cases.journey: A July 2024 release reported US$20m equity, US$60m debt commitments, more than 2,500 homes in 58 cities and 95 staff. An ADB project record states a US$20m loan and targets, not realised outcomes.
cases.monetization: Home sales and project finance rather than software subscriptions.
cases.result: The comparator is useful because capital structure and delivery burden are visible. It is not a YC graduate and not a margin proof.
cases.capital: Debt and equity are central. ADB targets must remain separate from homes actually delivered.
cases.failure_or_limit: No audited project margins or cohort delivery outcomes are in the selected sources.
cases.unknown: Whether Bangladesh land, approvals, finance and construction economics support a comparable model.
cases.transfer_test: Would a local housing test expose land, construction, finance and collection risk before software scale?

lenses.title: Why countries differ
lenses.question: Which conditions travel, and which must be rebuilt locally?
lenses.summary: Country is not a footnote. Records, licences, financing, agent density, payment rails, developer structure and data rights determine which mechanism can survive.
lenses.transfer: Bangladesh shares fragmented trust networks and developer-led supply with several comparators, but the missing evidence is close-level economics, rights-aware records and a repeatable collection path.

cases.name: Bangladesh
cases.mechanism: Fragmented discovery with public land-service workflows and an open price-data question
cases.customer: Developers, buyers, sellers, landlords, lenders and service operators.
cases.payer: Not yet established for a new JCX product. Existing brokerage or service fees are a separate local question.
cases.workflow: Property discovery, document and land-record checks, visits, negotiation, registration, mutation, handover, rent or service collection.
cases.human_burden: Document reconciliation, field checks, approvals, local trust, exception handling and collection.
cases.journey: The Ministry of Land explains khatian and the e-mutation portal shows application and download workflows. The IMF describes residential price-index development as an experimental process.
cases.monetization: A public source does not establish a repeatable payer, fee rule or collected commission for the proposed venture.
cases.result: The public evidence supports a bounded test, not a proven national platform.
cases.capital: The first burden is operating discipline and records, not a national interface or inventory balance sheet.
cases.failure_or_limit: No current public, quality-adjusted closing-price series or commercial reuse terms were established in the reviewed set.
cases.unknown: Mandate conversion, collection ageing, agent splits, document error rates and rival-developer neutrality.
cases.transfer_test: Can a named payer fund a small workflow that records inquiry, document, visit, close and collection events end to end?

cases.name: India
cases.mechanism: Large portal and developer-channel market with fragmented state records
cases.customer: Developers, agents, buyers, lenders and portal advertisers.
cases.payer: Portal advertising, developer distribution, brokerage or financial-service relationships.
cases.workflow: Search, developer project distribution, agent and lender coordination, plus state-level land and RERA records.
cases.human_burden: Local compliance, city density, project data and state-by-state record interpretation.
cases.journey: Info Edge reports 99acres segment results, while the IndianRERA directory shows a state and UT regulator structure. DILRMP remains a modernisation programme.
cases.monetization: Mature portal and distribution models exist, but India scale is not Bangladesh transfer evidence.
cases.result: The country shows that portal, channel and record layers can coexist without a single uniform rail.
cases.capital: Dense city operations, brand acquisition, compliance and working capital.
cases.failure_or_limit: State variation and local scale make national comparisons easy to overstate.
cases.unknown: Dhaka willingness to pay and equivalent record rights.
cases.transfer_test: Which city and property segment can support a paid, close-level workflow rather than a national directory?

cases.name: Pakistan
cases.mechanism: Provincial land-service digitisation with portal discovery
cases.customer: Landowners, buyers, public agencies and property-market participants.
cases.payer: Public service fees and private transaction or portal relationships.
cases.workflow: Fard, e-stamp, registry, mutation and valuation services are surfaced through provincial systems.
cases.human_burden: Provincial implementation, identity, document handling and local exceptions.
cases.journey: Punjab Land Records Authority publishes multiple land services and service-centre references.
cases.monetization: The cited source proves service surface, not private product margin or nationwide adoption.
cases.result: A public workflow can reduce a specific transaction bottleneck without creating a neutral national marketplace.
cases.capital: Government infrastructure and local service-centre operations.
cases.failure_or_limit: Punjab is not a country-wide proxy, and public service availability is not user-level outcome evidence.
cases.unknown: Bangladesh commercial access, service-level consistency and user willingness to pay.
cases.transfer_test: Which local land-service step is both legally usable and commercially supportable?

cases.name: Indonesia
cases.mechanism: Primary-market survey, platform services and electronic land-registration framework
cases.customer: Developers, buyers, renters, service customers and public agencies.
cases.payer: Developer, consumer, service and public data relationships.
cases.workflow: Property discovery and services sit alongside central-bank market surveys and an electronic land-registration legal framework.
cases.human_burden: Archipelago coverage, local service density, record integration and regulation.
cases.journey: Bank Indonesia publishes a residential property survey, and the 2023 regulation provides a legal basis for electronic land registration.
cases.monetization: The sources do not establish that a private platform captures the survey or registry economics.
cases.result: Digital infrastructure and market services can coexist while coverage and execution remain local.
cases.capital: Multi-city operations, service partners and integration.
cases.failure_or_limit: Regulation is not proof of uniform operational coverage.
cases.unknown: Dhaka data rights, provider density and service economics.
cases.transfer_test: Which local market signal can be joined to a paid workflow without mislabelling a survey as a transaction record?

cases.name: Vietnam
cases.mechanism: Land-use-right legal framework with implementation variation
cases.customer: Land users, developers, buyers, public agencies and professionals.
cases.payer: Transaction, professional and public-service relationships.
cases.workflow: Land-use rights, certificates, registration and local implementation shape the property process.
cases.human_burden: Legal interpretation, local administration, documents and exceptions.
cases.journey: The 2024 Land Law sets a framework for land-use rights and certificates.
cases.monetization: The legal source does not establish a startup's revenue or market outcome.
cases.result: Law can define a record and responsibility boundary, but implementation is still a country and local question.
cases.capital: Professional and administrative capacity rather than a simple app build.
cases.failure_or_limit: Legal framework does not prove clean data or an easy private access path.
cases.unknown: Bangladesh enforceability, data rights and local professional capacity.
cases.transfer_test: Which legal document or approval can a local partner verify with a named responsibility boundary?

cases.name: Philippines
cases.mechanism: Licensed real-estate service with developer and affordable-housing delivery
cases.customer: Buyers, developers, brokers, sellers and housing-finance partners.
cases.payer: Transaction and development economics under a professional licensing system.
cases.workflow: Licensed brokers and salespersons coordinate property transactions, while developers handle local delivery and financing.
cases.human_burden: Professional compliance, local field work, project delivery and collections.
cases.journey: The PRC publishes the real-estate service framework and a 2024 resolution references a broker-to-salesperson ratio. Lhoopa adds a capital-intensive delivery comparator.
cases.monetization: Licensing and developer or transaction payments are distinct from startup software revenue.
cases.result: A clear professional boundary can support a market, but it does not remove construction or collection risk.
cases.capital: Housing delivery uses debt and equity; brokerage uses people and licences.
cases.failure_or_limit: A regulatory ratio is not a productivity benchmark and Lhoopa targets are not realized outcomes.
cases.unknown: Bangladesh licensing, housing finance and field economics.
cases.transfer_test: Which professional role would be accountable for a JCX verification or closing workflow?

cases.name: Singapore
cases.mechanism: Government property-data API with defined update and transaction boundaries
cases.customer: Professionals, researchers, agencies and data products.
cases.payer: API or professional data users under access credentials and terms.
cases.workflow: URA exposes transaction records and a separate developer-sales service, with stated history and update frequency.
cases.human_burden: Government data governance, credentials, definitions and downstream interpretation.
cases.journey: The URA API reference covers five years of transaction records and publishes records at end of day each Tuesday and Friday. Its guidance separately recommends refreshing retained latest-five-year data daily because records can be modified or aborted. The developer-sales service is based on Options to Purchase.
cases.monetization: The public docs establish access and data boundaries, not downstream private margins.
cases.result: Separate services for resale and new-home data reduce category confusion. They do not make Bangladesh equivalent.
cases.capital: Institutional data rail and governance upstream of applications.
cases.failure_or_limit: Credentials, privacy, market structure and data completeness differ materially.
cases.unknown: A Bangladesh API or equivalent rights-aware dataset.
cases.transfer_test: Can Bangladesh keep asking, registered and developer-sales records separate in the product and the contract?

definitions.meaning: Gross transaction value, usually the value of transactions facilitated or recorded; it is not company revenue.
The amount recognised under the company's accounting policy; the payer, timing and gross or net presentation matter.
A defined management measure after selected variable costs; it is not automatically operating profit.
Use by the intended people or organisations under a stated denominator; a pilot, visit or download is not automatically adoption.
A bounded check with a source, date, identifier, responsible party and correction or liability boundary.
The next local evidence that would show whether a mechanism can work under Bangladesh's records, rules, density and payer conditions.

publicBoundary: No private JCX forecast, budget, operating record or internal criticism is included.
The venture remains a conditional experiment. The internal JCX adoption track is separate.
Foreign scale, funding, visits, listings, pilots and accelerator membership do not prove Bangladesh transfer.
A current public page proves product existence or a company statement, not repeat use, collected cash or profitability.
